transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (SterlingPay, Head of ML), Marcus Lee (SterlingPay, Platform), Sara Khan (SterlingPay, CTO)
---
Summary (auto): Quick demo of Redwood Optimize focusing on batching recommendations and prefix/KV cache cost model. Showed examples, latency tradeoffs, and a sample calc for 100 qps workload. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot.
---
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE, and with me is Priya, our SE who owns the Optimize flow. quick intro from the sterling team?
00:10 Lena: Hi, Lena Ortiz, head of ML at SterlingPay. we're looking at lowering inference cost for our fraud feature and also need tight 95th pctl latency for the 2-step chat flow.
00:25 Sara: Sara here, CTO — will be reviewing security and compliance but wanted to listen in.
00:31 Marcus: Marcus, infra — I'll help provide access if we go pilot.
00:35 Priya: Awesome. I'll run through batching, prefix and KV cache, and a cost model. We'll show a few numbers, and we can map to your 100 qps and 200-token average prompts.
00:48 Alex: Quick qual — are you currently using a hosted LLM provider or self-hosting?
00:52 Lena: We host on AWS, use a mix of finetuned open models and some 3rd-party APIs for chat. Running on g4/ g5 type instances.
01:05 Priya: Got it. So the main levers we'll talk about: batching (size / latency tradeoffs), prefix cache (for repeated prompt prefixes) and KV cache (long conversations / retrieval). We'll show how those affect tokens/server-hour and cost.
01:18 Priya: Slide — baseline: 100 qps, avg 200 tokens per request, ideal p95 < 300ms. If you run naively with single-request inference on a GPU you'll pay high token cost and miss p95 depending on model. Our Optimize tooling suggests continuous batching and prefix cache first.
01:35 Lena: What do you mean by prefix cache? is that like the embedding cache or more of a prompt template cache?
01:42 Priya: Good question. Prefix cache stores the KV cache for repeated prefixes — e.g., system prompt + instructions that are identical across users. That avoids re-computing early layers. For SterlingPay, if your fraud detection uses a standard prompt header for every request, prefix caching can serve that ~60-70% of cost savings for the early tokens.
01:58 Marcus: So this is kept in memory on the serving nodes? any extra infra?
02:02 Priya: It's in the serving runtime (we call it KV/prefix cache). It lives in GPU memory for hot prefixes; for larger footprint we spill to host memory and we have eviction policies. You can size it per model.
02:14 Sara: From security POV, is that encrypted? how do we control keys?
02:18 Alex: We integrate with KMS — either AWS KMS or customer HSM. The cache contents are ephemeral but checkpointed if you opt in; everything is logged to audit logs. We'll share SOC2 docs.
02:30 Lena: Good. Can you walk through the cost model? we need to compare to our current spend on dedicated GPU fleet.
02:35 Priya: Sure — quick whiteboard. Example numbers: baseline per-token infer cost on our hosted endpoint for model X is $0.0009 per token when running small batch sizes; with batching to 8 and prefix caching we show effective per-token cost drop to $0.00024. For your 100 qps, 200 tokens -> raw tokens/sec 20k -> monthly tokens ~52M. At baseline you'd be north of $46k/mo; with opt it's down to ~ $12k/mo. these are illustrative — we'll share the workbook.
03:10 Lena: Those are big numbers. how reliable are they across tail latency? our p95 requirement is strict.
03:16 Priya: Right. Batching helps throughput but increases latency if you wait too long for batch fill. We recommend adaptive batching: prefer small-max latency window (e.g., 30-50ms) and dynamic batch sizing based on load. For p95 <300ms we showed a config that keeps average batch size 4-6 at 100 qps which preserves p95 while still saving cost.
03:40 Marcus: How does dedicated vs hosted factor into this? We're concerned about noisy neighbors on shared pools.
03:45 Alex: For strict latency SLOs we recommend Redwood Dedicated — reserved GPU pools. That gives predictable throughput and you can pin models. However, hosted with routing policies and auto-fallbacks could also meet SLA depending on commitment. Dedicated usually wins for consistent p95.
03:58 Sara: If we need on-prem for compliance, is Redwood Private an option?
04:02 Alex: Yep, Private supports VPC and on-prem install; we can run the serving runtime in your environment and keep the control plane private. That's part of enterprise licensing. We'll include that options sheet.
04:15 Lena: Can you explain KV cache vs prefix cache again, and when to use each?
04:19 Priya: Sure — prefix cache is for deterministic repeated prefixes; KV cache (per-session) stores decoded KV states for each conversation so that long chat sessions avoid reprocessing. Use prefix cache for templated prompts across many users; use KV cache for long histories or retrieval augmentations. KV cache gives biggest wins when you have long context (~1k+ tokens) and repeat interactions.
04:36 Marcus: Is KV cache persisted across restarts? what's the consistency model?
04:40 Priya: It's ephemeral by default; you can configure persistent caches that checkpoint to storage with TTLs. Consistency is eventual for spill-to-host; we recommend hot-cache replication for critical sessions.
04:51 Lena: Any gotchas on memory footprint? we're worried about GPU memory being consumed by many sessions.
04:55 Priya: Yes — KV entries are per-session and increase memory. Optimize suggests a hybrid: prefix cache in GPU memory, KV cache in host/ssd with hot-session promotion. We provide tooling to simulate memory usage given session counts. We'll run your 2-week sim in the pilot.
05:15 Alex: quick demo — (screen-share) here's the Optimize workbook; you'll see tabs for batch policy, cache hit rate, cost per token. I can toggle prefix cache on/off and show delta.
05:30 Priya: (clicks) With prefix cache disabled: qps 100, avg batch 1.1, total tokens 52M, cost est $48k. Enable prefix cache and adaptive batching: effective tokens charged drop to 18M equivalent, cost est $13k, p95 stays ~260ms in this config.
06:02 Lena: That delta depends on prefix hit rate. What are realistic hit rates? our prompts vary a bit with customer-specific fields.
06:10 Priya: Right. If your prefix includes static system and instructions but variable fields later, you can still get 40-60% hit rate. We can add prefix templating so only the truly static chunk is cached. Also retrieval augmented prompts can be split so retrieval tokens are appended but base instruction cached.
06:30 Marcus: For the pilot, what's needed from our side?
06:33 Alex: We'll need sample workload (anonymized), VPC peering or API keys depending on hosting mode, and a success metric — e.g., 95th pctl <300ms with cost < $15k/mo equivalent.
06:45 Marcus: I can provision a test subnet and share peering info.
06:48 Sara: On security: SOC2, SSO, audit logs — we'll want the doc set.
06:52 Alex: We'll send SOC2 and our security pack after. Also details on KMS integration and data retention.
07:00 Priya: Back to batching knobs — we also recommend quantization profiles for models that support int8; that lowers GPU memory and increases effective batch sizes for same hardware. The cost model accounts for that as a separate line item.
07:18 Lena: Any reference customers that did this? shortcut examples?
07:21 Alex: We can share anonymized examples — e.g., Aurora Finance saw 60% token-cost reduction with prefix + KV hybrid and moved to Dedicated for 99.9% uptime. We'll share a 1-pager.
07:32 Lena: Sounds good. A couple technical Qs: how do you handle rate spikes? and what about cold-start penalties?
07:38 Priya: For spikes we have burst capacity options on Dedicated and routing policies on Hosted to fallback to a lower-cost model. Cold-start of a model can affect first requests — we use proactive pre-warm for pinned models. For the pilot we'll advise pinning the model on a small pool.
07:55 Marcus: Latency measurement — do you provide per-route p95 dashboards?
07:59 Alex: Yes, Redwood Console has per-route/model dashboards, token-level breakdowns and traces. We'll set up a dashboard for your pilot.
08:08 Lena: Ok next steps recap?
08:10 Alex: We'll: 1) Share pricing & pilot workbook (Alex + Priya) 2) Share SOC2/security docs (Alex) 3) Marcus to provide infra access details 4) Schedule a kickoff next week.
08:20 Sara: Good — we'll review and get back on approval.
08:23 Priya: I'll also include a short runbook for simulating memory and expected cache hit-rate with your dataset.
08:30 Lena: Thanks, this was helpful.
08:33 Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials.
---
Post-call notes: Agreed pilot that targets fraud feature and chat summarization. Primary success metrics: p95 <300ms and cost at or below $15k/mo equivalent. Action owners noted above. Resources to send: pricing sheet, optimize workbook, SOC2/security pack, pilot runbook, bench instructions.
